summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and a history of gastrointestinal bleeding presented with generalized weakness and chest pain after missing dialysis and experiencing severe diarrhea. He was found to have life-threatening hyperkalemia, which was treated with emergency dialysis. The chest pain was determined to be non-cardiac, likely musculoskeletal, with imaging showing a possible fracture of the left eighth rib. An inpatient capsule endoscopy was performed due to prior failed outpatient attempts, with results pending at discharge. His hand pain, following a fall, was attributed to soft tissue injury or gout flare. He remained stable throughout the admission, with improvement in electrolytes and symptoms, and was discharged home with follow-up plans for GI evaluation, blood sugar monitoring, and medication management.
